newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FORECAST-Malaysia April trade balance seen in deficit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Malaysia April trade balance seen in deficit.

text.p: Malaysia was expected to report an average trade deficit of 273.6 million ringgit ($108.8 million) in April, reversing the huge surplus reported a month ago, a Reuters poll of economists found.
The April trade deficit forecast compared with March's 1.75 billion ringgit surplus, and a 253.9 million ringgit shortfall in April a year ago.
But the estimates of the nine economists ranged widely, from a surplus of 50 million ringgit to a deficit of one billion ringgit, according to the poll, which was conducted on Wednesday and Thursday.
Analysts and foreign exchange dealers said there were rumours this week that the April gap would be as large as 2.0 billion ringgit.
The Statistics Department, which releases the monthly figures, does not have a fixed date on the data's release, though they are typically released in the second half of each month.
The economists said there were wide variations in the forecasts as they could not tell how many aircraft purchases would be included in the monthly data released by the Statistics Department.

"If they imported one plane it would cost around 500 million ringgit," said Sani Hamid, analyst at markets research firm MMS International. "I don't know why the market is talking about a big number. Unless they are talking about a delay in imports brought over from last month," he said.
Many economists said they did not expect the April deficit to be as large as rumoured.

"It's not possible for the trade balance to make a drastic downturn. Even if you take into account the purchase of two aircraft, that should not result in a two billion ringgit deficit unless there's a very significant drop in exports," said Mustafa Mohd Nor, chief economist at Arab-Malaysian Securities.
"This is not possible as exports have been improving steadily and there was no drastic change in global demand," he added.
But the economists said they did not expect to see March's huge surplus to be repeated this year, as imports would continue to outdistance exports.
Malaysia's booming economy continues to suck in capital and intermediate goods to feed the growth, they said.
The economy has chalked up above eight percent growth a year in the past nine years.
Malaysia recorded a negative trade balance of 618 million ringgit in 1996. The government has forecast that the balance would shrink to a deficit of 340 million this year.
"The big picture to me still points to downward pressure on the current account this year, despite favourable first-quarter numbers," said J.M. Sassoon chief economist Liew Yin Sze.
The government has forecast that the current account deficit will grow to 11.5 billion ringgit this year, from 11.0 billion in 1996.
Stockbrokers Thong & Kay Hian said the trade balance would be pressured for the rest of the year by the imports of "lumpy" items.
These include four Boeing 777-200s by Malaysian Airline System Bhd, five ships ordered by Malaysia International Shipping Corp Bhd and a number of fighter aircraft ordered by the government, it said.
"We expect a trend of worsening trade balance over the next three quarters, as more lumpy items are imported," Thong & Kay Hian said in a research note on Thursday.

The poll also found that economists expected an average broad money M3 growth of 20.4 percent for April, compared with 21 percent in March this year and 27 percent in April 1996. The M2 growth was seen at an average of 20.2 percent, against 20.8 percent in March and 27.9 percent in April last year.
($1= 2.515 ringgit)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
